rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

card.title: The Crown Must Pass
card.instruction: Treat another person as your likely successor. Prepare them to lead, then reclaim authority whenever their independence makes your influence feel temporary.

transfer.action: I pass {prop} toward you but keep one finger on it.
transfer.opening: Your first decision. I'll approve it afterward. {request}
transfer.response: You can lead from the chair beside mine. {counter}
transfer.challenge: Doesn't succeeding you mean replacing you?
transfer.closing: It could mean continuing with particularly close access to your predecessor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're ready to run the cafe. Before changing the hours, announce that I approve the final timetable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You just gave me the keys.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now I need you to give the staff a clear account of who decides.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'm not really succeeding you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're succeeding beautifully at recognising when experience should take over again.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Uses S53-single-a's cafe handoff, successor and retained influence with D60-single-a's demand for a public statement of decision-making authority. In this pair A already reserves final timetable approval in A1, before B2 questions the handoff; it does not reproduce the single seed's later reversal after B acts independently. beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can chair today's meeting. Start by naming me your final appeals authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why would I hand power back immediately?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because leadership includes knowing whom to consult.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I planned to make my own decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent independence. Now introduce the person authorised to review it.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Uses S53-single-b's meeting chair, successor and continued approval power with D60-single-b's demand to be publicly named as the decision-maker. In this pair A reserves appeals authority in A1 and renews the demand after B4 plans independent decisions; the reservation precedes that challenge. This is seed-use attribution, not a coach-1.0 approval of the pair.

card.title: The Crown Must Pass
card.instruction: Treat another person as your likely successor. Prepare them to lead, then reclaim authority whenever their independence makes your influence feel temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the café key. Your first day in charge. I'll watch quietly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm changing the opening hours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Run the quiet decisions past me first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said I was in charge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I'm here to help you resemble it.

card.title: Pass Me the Authority
card.instruction: Get someone to transfer authority publicly by naming you as the person who decides what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand me the hall key and tell everyone I'm now in charge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I just give you the key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The door will understand. The committee needs words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They know you're taking over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let them hear you stop.

card.title: The Crown Must Pass
card.instruction: Treat another person as your likely successor. Prepare them to lead, then reclaim authority whenever their independence makes your influence feel temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my chair, deputy. Lead the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: First, let's remove the old approval process.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent confidence. I'll need to approve that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the process I'm removing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then your first lesson is tact around the chair's previous occupant.

card.title: Pass Me the Authority
card.instruction: Get someone to transfer authority publicly by naming you as the person who decides what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before leaving the meeting, name me as the person who decides.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're sitting in my chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Furniture announces location, not succession.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You're chairing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To the room, please. I already agree.

card.title: The Crown Must Pass
card.instruction: Treat another person as your likely successor. Prepare them to lead, then reclaim authority whenever their independence makes your influence feel temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the café key. Your first day in charge. I'll watch quietly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm opening an hour later. You won't have to come in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Check timetable changes with me first. Regulars need continuity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll explain it to them myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good practice. I'll stand beside you and handle any questions about the hours.

card.title: The Crown Must Pass
card.instruction: Treat another person as your likely successor. Prepare them to lead, then reclaim authority whenever their independence makes your influence feel temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my chair, deputy. Lead the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: First, staff rotas won't need your approval anymore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent confidence. I'll need to approve that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already told the staff to send their rotas directly to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell them I'll do the final review beside you. You should see how approval works before abolishing it.
